items.title: fix(browser): return JSON for invalid tab indexes (#183603)
items.summary: fix(browser): return JSON for invalid tab indexes (#183603) fix(browser): print JSON errors for invalid browser tab indexes With --json, browser tab commands given an invalid tab index (for example `tabs select 0` or `tabs close abc`) exited 1 with nothing on stdout, which broke scripts reading the documented JSON error. They now print one standard cli_error JSON document; stderr, exit codes and the open tabs are unchanged. Evidence: built CLI against an authenticated Gateway with native Chromium and two local pages. On main both invalid commands printed nothing on stdout (twice each); with this change each prints a cli_error document (twice each), with stderr byte-identical and the tabs untouched. Valid select and close still act on the right tab, confirmed through CDP, and human-readable output is unchanged. Production +6/-1. Thanks @Leon-SK668. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi

items.title: fix(memory-core): split batches Mistral rejects for too many tokens o…
items.summary: fix(memory-core): split batches Mistral rejects for too many tokens overall (#183567) fix(memory): split embedding batches when a Mistral-compatible endpoint rejects the token total When a Mistral-compatible embedding endpoint rejected a batch because its total tokens were too large (HTTP 400, code 3210), memory indexing aborted instead of using the existing recursive split recovery that other providers already get. That rejection now triggers the same split, so the batch is retried in smaller parts; per-input and quota errors still fail as before. Evidence: built CLI with a local Mistral-compatible embedding fixture, indexing a file through shipped memory commands. On main a 6-input batch (7,434 characters) failed with 400/3210 and indexing aborted (twice); with this change it splits into 3 + 3, the file is indexed and shipped memory search finds it with vector score 1 (twice). A batch that keeps failing splits down to single inputs and then stops, and per-input and quota errors make one request each, as before. Production +4/-2. Thanks @lonexreb. Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi
